function.name: range_position
function.description: Where one reading of one LOINC sits against its Anchor v3 published range: below, within or above it, bounds inclusive. pick latest takes the newest reading in the window, pick at the reading at `at`. When the range depends on sex, age or timing, which the warehouse does not hold, position is null and depends_on names them; nothing is guessed. Reads up to 5000 rows; refuses no rows, mixed units, no published range, and a unit other than the range's (nothing is converted). Neutral position only.

start.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day

end.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that day

pick.description: latest: the newest reading in the window; at: the reading taken at `at`

at.description: With pick at only: the reading's effective_at as observations_for_subject returns it

function.name: convert_unit
function.description: Convert one value of glucose, creatinine, HbA1c, total/LDL/HDL cholesterol, triglycerides or body temperature between units with a fixed table: value rounded half away from zero, unrounded, unit, the formula used and the rounding rule. Reads no rows. A pair the table does not hold is refused with UNSUPPORTED_CONVERSION and the pairs it does hold.

function.name: cohort_position
function.description: Where a subject's latest value of one LOINC in a time range sits among the latest values, in the same window, of everyone in its synthetic cohort (one value per person, the subject included). percentile is the mid-rank percentile, 100 × (n_lower + n_equal / 2) / n, where n is the people with a value and n_equal counts the subject; say it as "higher than about <percentile> % of the <n> synthetic people with a value", never better, worse or normal. Synthetic cohorts only. Refuses no value for the subject, fewer than 10 people with a value, mixed units across the cohort, and more than 20000 cohort rows (narrow the window).

start.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day

end.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that day

function.name: conditions_timeline
function.description: List one subject's recorded conditions whose span overlaps the window (onset at or before its end, and no abatement or abatement at or after its start), oldest onset first: code_system, code, display, onset_at, abatement_at, clinical_status and verification_status as recorded (status as of the record, not of the window), with n, n_codes, by_status and n_without_abatement. Optional status and code narrow the list. Reads up to 1000 records; refuses more (ROW_CAP_EXCEEDED) and none (NO_ROWS, with the reason). Lists what is recorded; times relate as before or after, never as a cause.

start.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day

end.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that day

status.description: Only conditions with this recorded clinical status

code.description: One code as recorded (SNOMED CT or ICD-10 for conditions, RxNorm for medications)

function.name: medications_timeline
function.description: List one subject's recorded medication requests authored in the window, oldest first: code_system, code (RxNorm), display, authored_at, status and intent as recorded, and dosage_as_recorded, the record's own dosage text verbatim (null when the record has none), with n, n_codes, by_status and n_with_dosage_text. Optional status and code narrow the list. Reads up to 1000 records; refuses more (ROW_CAP_EXCEEDED) and none (NO_ROWS, with the reason). Lists what is recorded; never a dose, a change or advice of its own.

start.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day

end.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that day

status.description: Only medication requests with this recorded status

code.description: One code as recorded (SNOMED CT or ICD-10 for conditions, RxNorm for medications)

function.name: show_view
function.description: Show a view of one measure in the answer. chart.timeseries draws every reading in window; chart.compare sets window against compare_with (n and mean of each); biomarker.card shows a LOINC's latest reading against its published range, with its trend; table lists the readings (first 50). The server reads the rows itself; the result says how many it read. A LOINC code needs subject (a synthetic subject_ref); a wearable key reads the user's synced data. Never write numbers for a view yourself.

measure.description: A LOINC code, or a wearable key without its date, such as sleep.score

start.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day

end.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that day

window.description: Time window, ISO-8601 UTC or YYYY-MM-DD, start before end

subject.description: subject_ref for a LOINC code; leave out for wearable keys

compare_with.description: chart.compare only: the earlier window to set against window, such as the 4 weeks before it

start.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day

end.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that day

layout.description: chart.compare only: side-by-side (default) or overlaid by day of window

function.name: list_views
function.description: List the charts already shown in this thread, newest first: id, title, kind, model and time. Reads no data.

function.name: open_view
function.description: Show a chart from earlier in this thread again by its id from list_views. It is redrawn from the stored view with no new query; use it instead of show_view when the person asks to see a chart again.
